text:
We were very disturbed when we learned at the recent Governor Hathaway Recreation Action Team meeting that the National Forest Service had apparently received instructions from Washington that the open until closed philosophy was fine, but that the Bureau of Land Management had been told by Washington to work for a closed until open policy. This dichotomy of federal guidance is strange in itself, but frightening when the Bureau of Land Management and presumably the National Park Service is contemplating a course of action on the Washington level contrary to the suggestions of their local representatives, the Statewide Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan, and of sister federal agencies.
The following are general overall observations of the draft, etc., and hopefully will serve as a review of areas of concern with respect to the final product of this proposal.
There appears to be a difference in the titles between the Task Force Study and the Draft Environmental Statement which might be of some significance, i.e., the Task Force Study is entitled off-road Recreational vehicles and the Draft Environmental Statement indicates that all off-road vehicles, i.e., those used for agriculture and accdemic purposes, terrain mapping, administrative inspection, mineral prospecting, etc., are represented and included within the statement but not within the Task Force Study. In any case, there should be an addendum to the Statement concerning the effect of the proposal on these important non-recreation off-road vehicles. In connection with this, a study of the various conflict in laws involving the proposal and the established prospecting and mineral exploration laws, etc., should be carefully analyzed and effectively dealt with.
The definition of a road will also be of primary importance to the success of this proposal. With over 50 percent of Wyoming in federal ownership and potential roads involving everything from the dimmest game trail to Interstate Highways, it takes little imagination to think up problems of administration if the definition of a road is left nebulous.
Attached hereto please find a copy of the Draft upon which comments, suggested wordings, etc., have been made. .
